title: Branching out or bearing fruit: how MADS-box transcription factors orchestrate maize ovule development
content: New plant organs originate from meristems which contain a pool of pluripotent stem cells. Shoot apical meristem (SAM), root apical meristem (RAM) and floral meristem (FM) produce arial, underground, and floral tissues, respectively (Carles and Fletcher 2003; Perilli et al. 2012). In flowering plants, the formation of seed depends on timely transition of pluripotent FMs into specialized, determinate floral organs. The classical ABC(DE) model of floral development explains how varying combinations of transcription factors contribute to the identity of different parts of a flower (Bowman and Moyroud 2024). However, the point at which flowering development transitions from organogenesis to ovule formation, particularly in cereal crops, is not well understood.
